$comment: Every number here is a MEASURED baseline plus a stated headroom, never an
aspiration. Ratcheting these down is allowed only with a build report that
shows the new figure; raising one requires saying why in the same commit.
Sizes are gzip BYTES, because that is what a browser actually downloads.
Both the baseline and the current figures were produced by the same tool
(scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs, node zlib gzipSync) so they are directly
comparable. Vite's own console report prints identical byte counts in
decimal kB; the script matches that divisor for the same reason.
measuredAt: worktree wt/frontend-contracts, branched from main e3f9e37

baseline.$comment: Pre-split build, re-measured with gzipSync on a stashed tree so the reduction below is not a mix of two measurement methods.
baseline.note: One undivided chunk: 1,676.03 kB raw / 472.63 kB gzip JS plus 150.99 kB raw / 26.53 kB gzip CSS. Initial route fell 499,159 -> 106,972 bytes, a 78.6% reduction.

initialRouteGzip.rationale: Entry chunk plus every stylesheet and JS module the entry STATICALLY imports — what a cold visitor downloads before anything renders. Measured 106,972 bytes after the lazy split, down from 499,159. The headroom absorbs ordinary feature work without a budget edit; anything larger should arrive as a lazy leaf, not as entry growth.

maxChunkGzip.rationale: Largest single lazy chunk, currently NeuronUniverse at 162,283 bytes — effectively the cost of `three`, which exactly one file in src/ imports. A deliberate ceiling on any ONE surface, not a total. If a second chunk approaches it, the right response is usually another lazy boundary.

totalJsGzip.rationale: Sum across all JS chunks. Guards the failure mode the initial-route budget cannot see: shipping ever more code that merely happens to be deferred. Looser headroom than the other two because new lazy surfaces are the expected, healthy way for this number to grow.

notes: Not budgeted: dist/assets/corvus-logo-*.png (259.92 kB). It is an image, it is cached, and folding it in would let an unrelated art change break the JS gate.
The >500 kB raw-size warning Vite still prints applies to NeuronUniverse's chunk only. That is expected and is covered by maxChunkGzip; the pre-split warning covered the ENTIRE application.
